label: Intercompany governance
query: How should intercompany lending be governed so Lakeshore avoids sloppy AFR and true-up failures?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings, intercompany lending governance needs to be centralized at Holdco but executed through a disciplined, multi-opco spine: clear ownership, a single policy and data model, and automated controls integrated into each ERP (SAP S/4HANA at Holdco/Northline, SAP ECC/Coupa at Brightmark, NetSuite at Forge & Field and Great Lakes Pantry). Without that, you will keep seeing AFR noise and messy true-ups. Why 1) Fragmented ERP/process spine: your intercompany process is split across at least five ERP objects (ERP-LSH-HOLDCO-INTERCOMPANY on S/4HANA; ERP-NLS-INTERCOMPANY on S/4HANA with 11 customizations; ERP-BMS-INTERCOMPANY on SAP ECC/Coupa; ERP-FFF-INTERCOMPANY and ERP-GLP-INTERCOMPANY on NetSuite with 5 and 9 customizations). That screams “local workarounds,” which are exactly how AFR and true-up breaks are created. 2) Board and treasury priorities: board reporting and CFO guidance for 2025–2026 already call out “treasury visibility” and “systems fragmentation and renewal concentration” as risks, and Holdco’s cash forecast accuracy is still only 75%. Sloppy intercompany lending and late/incorrect true-ups directly degrade that KPI and your ability to deploy cash across 50 countries. 3) Holdco control spine mandate: your enterprise profile explicitly names a “Holdco control spine” under the Chairman / Global CIO / CFO for FY2026–2028. Intercompany lending is a core control-spine process; leaving policy, terms, and dispute-resolution to each opco finance/ERP team is inconsistent with that mandate.
